chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isa ibn al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who became junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) during the first part of the night in the month of Ramadan, and delayed the ritual bath (ghusl) until the dawn (fajr) broke. He said: 'He completes his fast, and there is no make-up (qada) required of him.'

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: Became junub (entered the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl)

ai.seo_question: Does delaying the ritual bath (ghusl) until after dawn invalidate the Ramadan fast?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Isfabar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that delaying ghusl until after Fajr does not invalidate the fast, distinguishing this state from one who eats or drinks intentionally. This ruling is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for determining the validity of Ramadan fasts when the state of janabah persists into the morning, emphasizing that the fast remains complete without requiring a separate qada (make-up) for this specific delay.
